chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Dāwūd al-Ṣirmī, who said: Bashīr ibn Yasār narrated to me, saying:
I asked him about salat (prayer) in khazz that is adulterated with the fur of rabbits, so he wrote: That is permissible.

So this is an anomalous report; none narrated it except Dāwūd al-Ṣirmī, even if it is repeated in the books with different chains. And it is possible that its basis is a form of taqiyyah, as we have stated regarding other reports.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: taqiyyah, precautionary dissimulation, proposed here as a possible explanation for the report
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual act whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.الْخَزِّ: khazz, a type of cloth or garment material discussed in legal rulings of prayer dress
key_terms.بِأَسَانِيدَ مُخْتَلِفَةٍ: with differing chains, referring to the report’s appearance through multiple lines of transmission
key_terms.خَبَرٌ شَاذٌّ: an anomalous report, a narration judged as isolated or irregular
key_terms.وَبَرِ الْأَرَانِبِ: rabbit fur, the material mixed into the garment and central to the ruling
key_terms.يَجُوزُ: it is permissible, the direct legal judgment given in the report

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) in khazz mixed with rabbit fur according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal ruling of performing salat (prayer) in khazz mixed with rabbit fur, stating permissibility in the narration itself. However, the compiler judges the report to be anomalous and suggests that it may have been issued under taqiyyah, showing the importance of hadith evaluation in deriving legal rulings.
